A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISC. Their text, figures, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite extensive rewriting, relocation, and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E report original benchmark results, ablations, and search analyses on APPS, MATH500, and LiveCodeBench.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen/R1 results, a sampled-reward histogram, and runtime-overhead measurements.

M1.justification: The core recursive decomposition and implementation in Appendices A–B are retained. v2 additionally proposes an optional variance/optimality-gap constraint on prefix acceptance in Appendix F, Remark 5. This would supplement the z-score criterion; its use in the reported experiments is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coding and mathematical tasks on APPS, MATH500, and LiveCodeBench. The self-generated validation-test setting already appears in v1. Qwen and R1 extend model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an explicit DeepSeek-R1 (Base) control against DeepSeek-R1 (DISC) in Figure 6. The existing TokenSplit, LineSplit, BoN, priority-variant, and greedy/beam/MCTS comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-7B and R1 evaluation configurations, including an R1 token-budget comparison matched to one base-model generation. It also introduces a 100-completion reward-distribution probe and runtime-share measurements. Existing benchmark subsets, principal metrics, and explicitly reported ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens supplementary validation through Qwen/R1 model analyses, the reward-distribution check supporting its distributional assumptions (Appendix C.5), and computational-overhead profiling (Appendix D.6). Existing temperature, priority, partition-fraction, self-validation, and search analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report per-step reward means and standard deviations. v2 adds no independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Its new 100-completion histogram examines reward distributions without establishing a changed replication or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds Qwen and R1 results; R1's base accuracy is approximately 0.28, while DISC reaches 0.52 with ten samples. Figure 43 newly reports 9.1% overhead for DISC. Existing benchmark curves are retained, although some newly added numerical summaries, including APPS pass@10 in Section 4.1, do not match the corresponding plotted values.

T1.justification: v2 adds optimality theorems, a probability-preservation lemma, proofs, and formal assumptions about reward distributions, variance contraction, and estimation accuracy in Section 3.3 and Appendix F. The Wiener-process example already appeared in v1 Section 3.4 and is relocated to Appendix F.2.

C1.justification: The original sample/token-efficiency claims remain. v2 expands the principal contributions to runtime efficiency, strong reasoning models, quantified error reductions and accuracy multipliers, and theoretical analysis of optimality. These extend the claimed scope beyond v1's empirical decomposition and critical-step findings.

C2.justification: The explanation for small partition fractions changes from asymmetric token-generation costs to avoiding irreversible commitment to poor prefixes. v2 also emphasizes incremental prefix commitment, interprets its reward histogram as supporting distributional assumptions, and explicitly qualifies optimality as dependent on strong, instance-specific policy assumptions.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states default partition fraction 0.15, reward threshold 1.0, and temperature 0.2, and adds API-access and single-A100-80GB hardware disclosures in Appendix G. New greedy-search and node-expansion pseudocode further specifies the existing framework, while the earlier implementation remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning LLM critics, LLM-as-a-judge, Forking Paths, s1, and long-chain-of-thought reasoning. It removes the Parascandolo et al. goal-directed-planning comparison. The main related-work categories and positioning in Section 5 remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The methodology is extensively rewritten around base and candidate prefixes, acceptance, and contraction. Experimental subsections are consolidated into main results, ablations, and interpretation. Notation and explanations change throughout, a contents section is added, and theoretical and impact material is reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to predominantly one column, redraws methodological diagrams, combines separate main-text plots into multipanel figures, and reorganizes appendix plots into grids. It also adds model, reward-distribution, and overhead graphics while retaining most existing plotted data.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, Qwen/R1 evidence, overhead profiling, and hardware disclosures are useful additions. However, the new optimality proof assumes retention of the best base sample, which the displayed pseudocode does not show, and its eventual-success argument is not reconciled with Algorithm 1's finite budget. New performance summaries also contain discrepancies with retained curves. These unresolved validity and reporting issues make the net quality effect uncertain.
